title: Optimization internship: SCUC research-to-engineering workflow
summary: Built and delivered a repeatedly tested UnitCommitment trajectory MVP covering startup/shutdown trajectory modeling, generator preprocessing, and automated Base/v1/v2 comparison tests. Also completed paper-to-code constraint mapping, subhourly conversion, and a documented instance-generation workflow. AI Coding tools assisted retrieval and drafting; key mappings and implementation details were manually verified.
boundaries: AI tools assisted retrieval and drafting; final verification was manual.
The public repository is an uploaded snapshot rather than a complete development history or full test-data archive.
The trajectory MVP was not deployed as a production power-system service.
Constraint mapping was comparison and documentation, not independent implementation of all mathematical constraints.
Do not claim that observed boundary behavior was fully resolved.

title: Optimization internship: Clarabel.cpp integration MVP for HiGHS
summary: As a final internship task, built and submitted a tested, AI-Coding-assisted Clarabel.cpp integration MVP in a HiGHS fork covering LP/QP data mapping, solution write-back, standalone and MIP root-LP routing, KKT quality gating, simplex fallback, targeted tests, regression checks, and a scoped SCUC benchmark.
boundaries: Repository artifacts prove the MVP exists but do not prove independent authorship of every line.
Benchmark results are limited to the recorded instances and configuration.
Submission and testing do not imply team adoption, upstream merge, production deployment, or production-grade stability.
Complete MVP refers to the agreed LP/QP and MIP-root integration scope; direct conic-problem APIs and broader cone support were deferred.

title: Optimization internship: SCIP heuristic analysis and RENS implementation
summary: Analyzed four SCIP MIP heuristics against HiGHS and produced data-structure mappings, architecture-difference analysis, mathematical abstractions, and flow diagrams. Implemented and tested only a SCIP-style RENS heuristic on HiGHS v1.12.0 against recorded MPS/MIPLIB cases.
boundaries: The SCIP-style RENS implementation was never committed or preserved after the version switch; only analysis documents, code excerpts, and test logs remain.
HiGHS already ships a separate native RENS implementation.
Shifting, Farkas Diving, and Pscost Diving were analyzed and abstracted, not implemented.
AI Coding assistance was used; do not claim independent authorship of every line.
Recorded tests do not establish production solver performance.

title: Data automation internship: REST API and Excel workflow
summary: Built a Python REST API workflow for a fixed set of market products, including specified-time Close collection, bid/ask means, token refresh, retry handling, multi-sheet Excel updates, derived indicators, cloud scheduling, daylight-saving handling, logs, and report emails.
boundaries: Runtime logs and report emails exist, but there is no independent monitoring or alerting system.
No pagination; scripts use fixed-interval throttling plus retry/token refresh, not full rate-limit governance.
No quantified efficiency improvement unless measured later.

title: C# internship: multimodal warehouse recommendation MVP
summary: Built an ASP.NET Core/C# warehouse-recommendation MVP whose candidate-confirmed runtime path uploads images to object storage, sends them to a logged-in multimodal web chat through browser automation, constrains item and dimension fields as JSON, and applies server-side warehouse rules with live-animal blocking, custom validation, and manual fallback.
boundaries: Did not train a vision model.
The browser runtime path is candidate-confirmed; its old source is missing.
A surviving API implementation was not the running internship path.
The earlier MVP was candidate-reported as demoable and tested on a small scale, not proven production-grade.

title: AI Chinese learning mini program and Coze agents
summary: As a primary technical team member, developed login, registration, learning-center, and child pages for a WeChat mini program; participated in authentication API integration and fixed mismatches across variable names, database fields, and page references. Translated essay-correction and learner-level dialogue requirements into reviewed prompts and configured the corresponding Coze agents.
boundaries: AI Coding tools assisted page implementation and prompt drafting.
Later completion involved external development support.
Do not claim full production system ownership.
The authentication flow was not load-tested or production-validated.
The Coze work was prompt and platform configuration, not a custom multi-node Agent architecture.

title: Emotion pixel visualization: LLM pipeline and CLIP evaluation
summary: Built a pipeline using DeepSeek-Chat for structured emotion extraction and DALL-E 3 / ChatGPT Images (gpt-image-2) for image generation, mapping Chinese text to emotion JSON and then visual generation conditions. Designed prompt compression and evaluated image-text alignment on 10 samples with CLIP ViT-B/32: Baseline 0.2530, Partial 0.2163, and Full 0.2593; Full beat Partial on 9/10 samples but improved only 2.5% over the Baseline mean and beat Baseline on 5/10 samples.
boundaries: Application/evaluation project, not large-scale model training.
The CLIP evaluation used 10 samples and a Wilcoxon signed-rank analysis; treat the results as exploratory rather than a statistically conclusive performance claim.
Full improved the mean CLIP score by only 2.5% over Baseline and beat Baseline on 5/10 samples; do not claim a broad or significant improvement.

title: DL-Learning-Lab: deep learning and visual generation learning project
summary: Completed PyTorch experiments covering DDPM/CFG, Stable Diffusion LoRA, SegFormer, and related notes.
boundaries: Learning/open-source practice, not a research publication or enterprise production result.

title: Truthful Resume Agent: JD matching and fact-gated resume CLI
summary: Built a local Python CLI and FastAPI Web UI that save public JDs, match them against a structured personal fact bank, generate match reports and review sheets, require candidate-run A/B/C/D confirmation before resume generation, and output Markdown/HTML JD insight reports plus LaTeX resume drafts. The CLI includes analyze, gap-check, and career-trends workflows, while resume ordering and section limits are separated into configuration and selected by job type.
boundaries: Personal/local CLI workflow, not a multi-user SaaS product.
Does not autonomously decide whether an experience is true; the candidate must run decide and confirm A/B/C/D.
Does not automatically submit resumes or write unconfirmed LLM output into delivered resumes.
Interactive confirmation markers are a friction barrier, not cryptographic proof of human authorship.

title: Truthful Resume Agent: Qdrant semantic retrieval and bounded RAG phrasing
source_section: Public semantic retrieval and JD Insight workflow
summary: Replaced a JSON embedding cache with a local embedded Qdrant vector database for fact-chunk semantic retrieval, then built a bounded RAG phrasing step in explain-jd: retrieved JD-matched facts are sent to DeepSeek for phrasing candidates, and each candidate is rejected unless its fact_id is in the matched set and a separate boundary check confirms the sentence does not exceed the cited fact.
boundaries: Local embedded Qdrant collection over a small personal fact bank, not large-scale vector database tuning.
Chunking is one structured fact record per chunk; the project does not implement long-document parsing, recursive splitting, or a reranking stage.
fastembed uses an ONNX-backed embedding runtime internally, but this project does not include direct model conversion, quantization, edge deployment, or ONNX Runtime performance tuning.
RAG is used for bounded phrasing candidates in a JD insight report, not for autonomously generating final resume bullets.
No LlamaIndex, MCP, vLLM, Ollama, KV-cache optimization, SFT, or RL implementation.
Does not implement a production knowledge-base system with external document ingestion, access control, monitoring, or multi-user serving.

title: Truthful Resume Agent: LangGraph conversational fact agent
summary: Built a read-only LangChain and LangGraph fact agent with a retrieve-to-generate-to-verify-to-reflect StateGraph loop, fact search and verification tools, a FastAPI conversation API, UUID-isolated SQLite checkpoints, bounded LLM timeout and retry handling, sanitized node traces, and fixed workflow regression cases.
boundaries: Personal/local fact Q&A service, not a multi-user assistant with authentication, distributed execution, or external production monitoring.
The agent retrieves and explains existing facts; it does not write facts, review decisions, or resume wording.
The verification node is an LLM judgment rather than cryptographic proof.
The API uses a local SQLite checkpointer, while the REPL can still use MemorySaver; cross-session preferences use a separate local JSON file.
SQLite checkpoints contain conversation state and evidence; the separate trace tables exclude raw chat, JD, resume text, provider bodies, and API keys.
Timeouts and transient retries are bounded, but no distributed queue, circuit breaker, or availability SLA is implemented.
